threads.thread_goal: Align on scope and approve target chart of accounts for relocation jobs.

messages.text: Kicking off the Standardised Accounting and Move-Cost Tracking for Relocation Jobs project. I have uploaded the first draft of the relocation chart of accounts as Relocation Chart of Accounts Specification and linked it to our initial task to draft the relocation-focused structure. This is our working version of A1 and ties directly to T1. The draft introduces separate revenue and cost accounts for standard moves, storage, and dangerous goods surcharges, plus a relocation segment view for reporting. Please review with two questions in mind: 1) Are we capturing all relocation activities that need separate lines? 2) Are any of the proposed accounts likely to clash with how you currently post jobs? I would like initial comments today so we can iterate quickly and still hit the 21-day go-live.

Thanks for sharing the draft. From a day-to-day posting angle, I like that we have separate direct cost accounts for labour, transport, and dangerous goods handling. One thing I want to double-check: for dangerous goods, do we want a single surcharge revenue account, or should we split between packing, storage, and transport surcharges? That will affect how we track compliance costs later. Also, I did not see a suspense account specifically for incomplete relocation job data; should that sit under the general suspense, or do we want a relocation-specific one in A1?

I went through the revenue section in A1 and compared it with how I currently post moves. I see lines for domestic relocation, international relocation, storage, and dangerous goods surcharge. We also sometimes bill separate fees for weekend work and after-hours access. Do we want those as separate relocation revenue accounts, or should they stay under general other income? It might help management to see those separately when they look at job profitability.

I have a question on the cost side of A1. For transport costs, we have separate accounts for internal fleet and third-party carriers. For dangerous goods, should we mirror that split, or is one combined dangerous goods transport cost account enough? From my mover days, the carrier invoices for dangerous goods can be quite different from standard freight, so I am leaning toward separate accounts to keep reconciliations cleaner.

I started looking at A1 but I am not totally sure how to map some of the current codes. For example, we have a generic packing materials account we use for all jobs. In the new structure, there is a relocation packing materials account and a dangerous goods packing materials account. Do we need to move all packing for relocation jobs into the relocation account, or only new jobs after go-live? And for the current fiscal year limit, do we reclass old postings or leave them as is?

I saw the new relocation revenue accounts in A1. Does this mean we stop using the old general moving revenue account completely? I am a bit worried about changing codes in the accounting system and breaking existing reports. Maybe we can keep posting to the old account and just tag jobs as relocation somehow?

On dangerous goods surcharges, I propose we keep one surcharge revenue account but use subcategories in the job costing template later to distinguish packing, storage, and transport. That keeps A1 lean while still giving us detail in A3. For suspense, I agree we should have a relocation-specific suspense account for incomplete job data so we can monitor it closely. I will add a relocation job suspense account to A1 and flag it in T1 as part of the final structure.

Good catch on weekend and after-hours fees. Given management wants visibility into profitability per move and service type, I suggest we add a relocation premium services revenue account that covers weekend, after-hours, and similar surcharges. We can document examples in A1 so everyone posts consistently. That would mean these activities are tracked separately rather than buried in other income.

Agree on splitting dangerous goods transport costs between internal fleet and third-party carriers. It will help when we reconcile carrier invoices and also when we explain variances to the finance manager. I will update A1 to include two separate dangerous goods transport cost accounts and note the usage rules under T1 so we remember to walk through examples during training.

For packing materials, I would suggest we only move new postings for relocation jobs into the new relocation packing materials account after go-live. For the current fiscal year, we can do a limited reclass for larger relocation jobs if the finance manager wants better comparatives, but we should not try to restate everything. That keeps us within the current-year-only constraint and avoids too much rework. We can document this cut-over rule in A1 under the account description.

We do need to move away from the old general moving revenue account for new relocation jobs, otherwise we will not get the relocation segment view we need. To reduce risk, we will not delete the old account; we will just stop using it for new relocation postings and keep it for legacy items. In T5 we will only update categories and mappings, no structural system changes, and we will test sample postings to confirm reports still work. If anything looks off, we will involve the finance manager before finalising.

Relocation premium services revenue account sounds good to me. That will make it easier when we prepare sample monthly financial statements later, because we can show how much of the margin comes from these extras. Maybe we can also add a short note in A1 with typical invoice line descriptions that should map there, so we do not classify random admin fees as premium services by mistake.

With the extra dangerous goods transport accounts added, I think the cost side of A1 covers what we see in practice: labour, fleet, third-party carriers, packing materials, storage, and surcharges. The only other thing I can think of is specific permits or inspection fees for dangerous goods. Do we want a separate account for those, or should they sit under general regulatory fees?

Got it, so for packing materials I will start using the relocation packing materials account only for new relocation jobs after go-live, and we might do a limited reclass for big jobs if asked. Can we add a simple example in A1, like one line showing old account and one showing new account, so it is clear during training?

Thanks, that makes sense. Keeping the old revenue account but not using it for new relocation jobs feels safer. When we get to configuring the accounting system under T5, I might need a walkthrough on how to change the mappings without touching the structure, but I can follow a step-by-step if we document it.

Good point on permits and inspection fees. Given the compliance focus for dangerous goods, I suggest we add a dedicated dangerous goods permits and inspection fees account under relocation direct costs. That will help when we later align with the health and safety officer and external auditor on evidence. I will update A1 accordingly.

Yes, adding a simple before and after example in A1 is a good idea. We can also reuse that example later in the quick-reference posting guide so people see the same pattern in both places. I will draft a short example and share it with you for a quick check before we add it.

To summarise where we have landed so far: 1) We will have separate relocation revenue accounts for domestic, international, storage, dangerous goods surcharge, and premium services such as weekend and after-hours work. 2) On the cost side, we will split dangerous goods transport between internal fleet and third-party carriers, add a relocation job suspense account, and create a specific account for dangerous goods permits and inspection fees. 3) We will stop using the old general moving revenue account for new relocation jobs after go-live but keep it for legacy postings, and we will only restate selected current-year items where it is worth the effort. Unless anyone objects by tomorrow midday, I will treat this as approval of the proposed relocation chart of accounts in A1 and confirm that the relocation activities listed above are the ones we will track on separate lines.
The summary matches my understanding, and I am comfortable with the list of relocation activities that will have separate lines. No further comments from me on A1.
Same here, the structure you described covers what we need for day-to-day posting and later job costing. I support moving ahead with this version of A1 so we can start on the downstream tasks.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise the relocation accounting SOP, including handover.

messages.text: I have posted the first full draft of the Relocation Accounting SOP as A2. It covers the end-to-end flow from job creation through invoicing and month-end, including specific steps for dangerous goods surcharges and the new relocation accounts from A1. This draft also links to our tasks T2 and T12. Please read with a focus on two points: 1) Does the posting flow match how jobs actually move from operations to us? 2) Is the minimum data set from operations clear enough so we can post without chasing extra details every time? I would like comments by end of day so we can refine and then run it past operations and health and safety.

I went through A2 and the overall flow looks sensible: job created in the operations system, minimum data set captured, handover to accounting, then postings at key milestones. One question: for dangerous goods, you mention an extra check against the Dangerous Goods Accounting Compliance Guide. Should we explicitly reference A5 in the SOP so people know where to look for the statutory obligations and evidence requirements?

On the handover section in A2, the minimum data set from operations currently lists customer name, job ID, origin, destination, estimated move date, and whether dangerous goods are involved. In practice, we also need at least an estimate of labour hours and transport type to set up the job costing template correctly. Should we add those to the minimum data set in T12 so we are not guessing later?

I am reading through A2 and I am a bit confused about when we post deposits. The SOP says we post a deposit when the job is confirmed, but sometimes customers pay only a few days before the move. Do we always wait for the payment to hit the bank before posting, or do we post a receivable when the job is confirmed and then clear it when the deposit arrives?

In the handover checklist in A2, it says operations will send us a daily file by 3pm. Right now I usually get job details by email at random times. Do we already have this daily file set up with the relocation coordinators, or is that something we still need to agree under T12?

Yes, we should explicitly reference the Dangerous Goods Accounting Compliance Guide in A2. I suggest we add a short step in the dangerous goods section: check A5 for required evidence and attach the relevant documents to the job file before month-end. That will make it easier when we later prepare the audit evidence pack.

Agree on adding labour hours estimate and transport type to the minimum data set. Without those, we end up adjusting the job costing template later. I will update the T12 definition so the minimum data set includes: job ID, customer, origin, destination, move date, dangerous goods flag, estimated labour hours, and transport type (internal fleet vs carrier). We can still refine this with operations, but it gives us a clear baseline.

On deposits, I would keep it simple: we only post a deposit when cash actually hits the bank. Before that, the confirmed job just sits as an open job in operations. Once the deposit arrives, we post it to the relocation deposits liability account and then clear it against the final invoice. We can add a short example in A2 to show the sequence and make sure it lines up with the reconciliation checklist in A4.

The daily file from relocation coordinators is not in place yet; what you see in A2 is the target process. Under T12 we still need to agree with operations on the file format and the 3pm cut-off. I will draft a simple template for the daily file and then we can walk through it with a coordinator to confirm it is realistic.

That minimum data set works for me. With labour hours and transport type included, we can set up the job costing template A3 on day one instead of waiting for extra info. Maybe we should also note in A2 that if labour hours change significantly, operations should update the daily file so we can adjust before invoicing.

Thanks, that clarifies deposits. So we only post when the money is in the bank, to the relocation deposits liability account, and then clear it when we issue the final invoice. An example in A2 would help me remember the steps, especially how it shows up in the reconciliation checklist.

Understood. Once you have a draft of the daily file template, I am happy to test it for a couple of days by filling it in manually from the emails I get, just to see if anything is missing before we ask operations to adopt it.

I reviewed the full posting flow in A2 from job creation to month-end. The sequence of events and postings looks consistent with how we work, with the additions we just discussed: explicit reference to A5 for dangerous goods checks, clarified deposit handling, and the updated minimum data set. I do not see any gaps that would block us from processing jobs under the new chart of accounts.

Thanks for all the input. I will now update A2 to: 1) Add an explicit step to consult A5 for dangerous goods evidence and link it to the audit pack. 2) Clarify that deposits are posted only when cash is received, with an example that ties into A4. 3) Lock in the minimum data set from operations as job ID, customer, origin, destination, move date, dangerous goods flag, estimated labour hours, and transport type, plus a note that significant changes should be updated before invoicing. Once I have made these edits, I will share A2 with the operations manager and health and safety officer for validation. Unless there are objections, we can treat this as agreement on the end-to-end posting flow and on the minimum data set.

threads.thread_goal: Design and validate the job costing template and reconciliation checklist.

messages.text: I have uploaded initial versions of the Relocation Job Costing Template and the Monthly Relocation Accounts Reconciliation Checklist as A3 and A4. These drafts are linked to T3 and T4. A3 is structured to capture revenue, labour, transport, dangerous goods costs, and permits per job, aligned with the accounts we agreed in A1. A4 lists the monthly checks for bank, revenue, cost, deposits, and suspense accounts. Please review and comment on: 1) Any missing fields in A3 that you need for job profitability. 2) Any reconciliation steps in A4 that are unclear or unrealistic given our current tools.

Looking at A3, the main sections make sense: job header, revenue lines, labour, transport, dangerous goods, and other direct costs. I would add a simple flag for whether the job is part of a corporate contract or a one-off private move, since that often affects pricing and margin. On A4, the reconciliation step for dangerous goods permits suggests checking every job individually each month. That might be heavy; maybe we can sample by carrier or by month instead, as long as it still satisfies audit expectations.

In A3, under labour, we have fields for estimated hours and actual hours. Could we also add a field for overtime hours specifically? For weekend and after-hours jobs, it would help to see how much of the labour cost is overtime versus standard time, especially since we now have a premium services revenue account in A1.

On A4, the step about reconciling relocation deposits suggests matching every deposit to a job ID and then to the final invoice. That is ideal, but in practice we sometimes get bank references that do not clearly show the job ID. Should we include a note about how to handle unidentified deposits, maybe by parking them in a temporary relocation suspense account until we can match them?

I tried filling in A3 for a recent domestic move. I was not sure where to put tolls and parking fees for the truck. There is a transport cost section, but the examples mention fuel and carrier invoices. Should tolls and parking go under transport, or under other direct costs?

On A4, the bank reconciliation step says we should agree the relocation bank sub-ledger to the main bank account. I usually just check the main bank reconciliation report. Do we have a separate relocation bank sub-ledger already, or is that something we will set up when we configure the system under T5?

Good idea on the corporate vs private flag. I will add a simple dropdown in A3 for contract type so we can filter later. For the dangerous goods permits check in A4, I agree that checking every job monthly is heavy. I suggest we define a sampling approach: for example, each month we pick a sample of dangerous goods jobs by carrier and confirm permits and fees against A5. We can then document this sampling method in A4 and confirm with the external auditor when we finalise A8.

Yes, adding an overtime hours field in the labour section of A3 makes sense, especially now that we track premium services revenue separately. We can then compare overtime cost against premium revenue when we analyse job profitability. I will add that field and include a short note on how to capture it from timesheets.

For unidentified deposits, I would route them to the relocation job suspense account we added in A1 until we can match them to a job. In A4 we can add a step under deposits to review any balances in that suspense account monthly and either match them or escalate. That way we do not lose track of them.

Tolls and parking should go under transport costs in A3, since they are directly linked to moving the truck. I will update the examples in the transport section to list tolls and parking explicitly so it is clear. That will also align with the transport cost accounts in A1.

We do not have a separate relocation bank sub-ledger today. What A4 is aiming at is more of a relocation-specific view of bank movements related to relocation accounts. When we work on T5, we can set up categories or reports that filter bank entries linked to relocation jobs. In the meantime, we can adjust the wording in A4 to say we reconcile relocation-related bank movements using the main bank reconciliation plus a relocation filter, rather than a separate sub-ledger.
Thanks, that helps. I will put tolls and parking under transport in A3 from now on. The extra examples will make it easier when we test the template on more jobs.

Using the relocation job suspense account for unidentified deposits and then reviewing it monthly in A4 sounds good. That will also make it easier to explain any remaining balances to the finance manager during month-end reviews.

I have now tested A3 on three recent jobs: one domestic, one international, and one dangerous goods move. The template captured revenue, labour (including overtime), transport, dangerous goods surcharges, and permits without needing extra columns. The only adjustment I made was adding the contract type flag we discussed. Based on this, I am comfortable that the structure and fields in A3 are fit for purpose.

From my side, A4 now covers the key monthly checks: bank movements linked to relocation, revenue and cost accounts including dangerous goods, deposits and the relocation suspense account, plus a sampling check for dangerous goods permits tied back to A5. The wording around the bank reconciliation is clearer with the filter approach. I think this checklist is workable for month-end.

To close this out: 1) We will proceed with A3 including the contract type flag, overtime hours field, and clarified examples for transport costs such as tolls and parking. 2) We will use A4 as the standard monthly reconciliation checklist, with the relocation suspense account for unidentified deposits and a sampling approach for dangerous goods permits aligned with A5 and future audit expectations. I will mark T3 and T4 as ready for final review once these edits are in.

threads.thread_goal: Plan and debrief the pilot of the new process on selected jobs.

messages.text: We are ready to start the pilot of the new relocation accounting process. From today, we will process a limited set of jobs using the new SOP in A2 and the job costing template A3 under T10. I have created the Pilot Jobs Issue Log as A7 so we can capture any problems or questions as we go. For the pilot, we will use the updated chart of accounts and mappings once T5 is configured for the selected jobs only. Please log issues in A7 as you encounter them, and use this thread to flag anything that might block us.

I have just processed the first pilot job, a domestic move with no dangerous goods, using A2 and A3. Overall it went smoothly, but I noticed that the system mapping under T5 still defaulted one revenue line to the old general moving revenue account. I corrected it manually and logged the issue in A7. We should adjust that mapping before we scale up.

I ran a dangerous goods job through the pilot. The SOP in A2 worked, but I had to chase operations for the permits because they were not attached to the job file. I logged this in A7 as a handover issue. Maybe we need a stronger reminder in the daily file template that dangerous goods jobs must include permit copies before we can finalise postings.

I tried to use A3 for a storage-only relocation job. I was not sure how to handle monthly storage fees versus the initial move-in. I put the initial move-in under transport and the monthly storage fees under other direct costs, but it felt a bit clumsy. I added this as an issue in A7 in case we want a clearer pattern.

I processed one small domestic job in the pilot. The daily file from operations came through, but it was missing the transport type field, so I had to guess whether it was internal fleet or carrier. I logged this in A7. Maybe the coordinators need a quick reminder on filling in all the fields.

Thanks for catching the mapping issue. I will review the configuration under T5 and update the product-to-account mapping so that all relocation revenue lines for pilot jobs point to the new relocation revenue accounts. Once updated, I will run a couple of test postings and note the results in A7.

On the dangerous goods permits, I agree we need a stronger control. I will update the daily file template under T12 to include a mandatory field indicating that permits are attached, and we can add a step in A2 that says we do not finalise postings for dangerous goods jobs until the permits are in the job file. I will also add a reminder in A7 so we track any exceptions during the pilot.

For storage-only jobs, I suggest we treat the initial move-in as a standard transport cost and the recurring storage fees as a separate storage revenue and storage cost line in A3. I will adjust the template to make storage a distinct section with examples, so it is clearer. I will also update A7 to show how we want these jobs handled going forward.

Missing transport type in the daily file is a good example of where the new process depends on operations. Maybe for the rest of the pilot we can do a quick daily check with one relocation coordinator to confirm any blanks, and we can use those examples in training later. I will add a note in A7 and propose this as a temporary workaround.

That sounds good. If the daily file clearly shows whether permits are attached, it will save us time. During the pilot I can keep an eye on any dangerous goods jobs where the field is blank and log them in A7 so we have data when we talk to the health and safety officer.
Thanks, making storage its own section in A3 will help. I will re-enter the storage-only job using the new layout once it is updated and add a note in A7 if anything still feels unclear.
I can do that daily check with a coordinator during the pilot. I will keep a small list of jobs where I had to confirm transport type and log them in A7 so we can see if the issue reduces over time.

Quick mid-pilot update: we have processed five jobs under T10 so far (mix of domestic, international, dangerous goods, and storage). Issues logged in A7 fall into three main buckets: 1) System mappings still pointing to old revenue accounts for some products. 2) Incomplete data in the daily file, mainly missing transport type and permit attachments. 3) Some confusion on storage-only job layout in A3, which we are addressing with a clearer section. None of these have blocked us from posting, but they would cause noise if we rolled out to all jobs immediately.

From what I have seen in A7, the mapping issues under T5 and the daily file gaps under T12 are the main items we should fix before a full rollout. The storage layout in A3 is more of a usability tweak and can be refined even after go-live as long as the accounts are correct. I would prioritise: 1) Fixing all remaining mappings for relocation revenue and dangerous goods surcharges. 2) Agreeing with operations on the daily file fields and the rule that dangerous goods jobs must include permits before month-end.

I agree with that prioritisation. Once the mappings and daily file are stable, the remaining issues in A7 look manageable as part of normal continuous improvement. Based on the five pilot jobs, I do not see any fundamental problems with A2 or A3 that would stop us from using them more broadly, as long as we close those two items first.

Given the pilot results so far and the issues logged in A7, my view is that we can proceed to full rollout once we: 1) Correct the remaining system mappings under T5 for relocation revenue and dangerous goods surcharges. 2) Finalise the daily file template and permit requirement with operations under T12. These are both in progress and should be achievable within the next few days. With those conditions met, I would recommend a go decision for rollout rather than extending the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Prepare training, quick-reference materials, and audit evidence pack.

messages.text: With the pilot nearing completion, I have drafted two key documents: 1) The Bookkeeper Quick-Reference Posting Guide as A6, linked to T8. 2) The External Audit Evidence Pack for Relocation Accounts as A8, linked to T11. A6 is a one-page summary of posting rules with examples, and A8 lists the standard reports and documents we will keep for audits, including references to A2, A3, A4, and A5. I have also sketched a training session outline under T9. Please review A6 for clarity and completeness, and A8 for whether the evidence list is realistic for us to maintain.

On A6, I like the layout with the main posting patterns and the small examples. One suggestion: can we add a short section on common errors we saw during the pilot, such as using the old revenue account or misclassifying storage-only jobs, and how to correct them? That would help people avoid repeating the same mistakes.

For A8, the list of evidence includes job costing templates for all relocation jobs. That might be heavy if we have to store every single A3 separately. Could we instead keep A3 for a sample of jobs per month and rely on system reports for the rest, as long as the system data is complete? We should check what the external auditor expects under T11, but I want to make sure the pack is sustainable.

On the training session under T9, I suggest we structure it around three flows: 1) Standard domestic or international job. 2) Dangerous goods job, with emphasis on A5 and permit evidence. 3) Storage-only or storage-heavy jobs. We can use A6 as the handout and walk through real examples from the pilot, referencing A7 where we had issues.

I read A6 and it is very helpful. The only part I struggled with is the section on deposits and how they clear against the final invoice. Maybe we can add a small diagram or a step-by-step example showing the deposit posting, the final invoice, and the reconciliation step in A4.
For the training session, could we record it and store the recording link in A6 or A2? I might not be able to join live, but I want to make sure I can go back and watch the walkthroughs.

Good idea. I will add a short common errors section to A6 based on A7, covering at least: using the old revenue account, missing transport type, and storage-only job layout. For each, we can show the incorrect posting and the corrected one, so people can fix entries if they spot them.

On A8, I agree that storing every single A3 might be overkill. I propose we keep full A3 templates for a defined sample of jobs each month, for example the top five by revenue plus all dangerous goods jobs, and rely on system reports for the rest. We will confirm this sampling approach with the external auditor under T11 and update A8 accordingly.

I like the three-flow structure for the training. We can build the agenda in T9 around those flows and use A6 as the main reference. For the dangerous goods part, we should show exactly where A5 fits in and how the permit evidence ends up in the audit pack A8.

I can add a simple step-by-step example in A6 for deposits: 1) Post deposit to the relocation deposits liability account when cash is received. 2) Post the final invoice to revenue and receivables. 3) Apply the deposit against the invoice and show how it appears in the reconciliation checklist in A4. A small diagram should make this clearer.

Yes, we will record the training session and add the link to both A2 and A6 so it is easy to find. Under T9 we will also capture any open questions raised during the session and update A6 or A2 if needed.

The sampling approach for A3 in A8 sounds reasonable. Focusing on the largest jobs and all dangerous goods jobs should give the auditor enough detail without overloading us. Once we have their feedback under T11, we can lock in the final list.

I have reviewed A6 end to end with the planned additions. It covers the main posting rules, examples for standard, dangerous goods, and storage jobs, the deposit flow, and the common errors from A7. I think it is ready to use as our standard quick-reference guide.

On A8, with the sampling approach for A3, the inclusion of the SOP A2, job costing template A3, reconciliation checklist A4, and dangerous goods guide A5, plus bank and ledger reports, I believe we have a solid baseline for audit evidence. I will walk this through with the external auditor under T11, but from our side I am comfortable treating this as the final list unless they request minor tweaks.

To wrap this up: 1) We will finalise A6 with the common errors section, deposit example, and references to the training recording. 2) We will proceed with A8 using the sampling approach for A3 and the core documents A2, A3, A4, and A5, and then confirm with the external auditor under T11. 3) For T9, I will schedule a one-hour training session covering the three flows we discussed and share the invite shortly. Once the session is done, we will update A6 and A2 with any clarifications that come out of the Q&A.
